## Building a New PC – A Step‑by‑Step Guide Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough that covers everything from choosing parts to installing the operating system. Feel free to skip sections that you already know or dive deeper into the ones that interest you. --- ### 1. Plan Your Build | Question | Why it matters | Tips | |----------|----------------|------| | **What will you use it for?** | Determines CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, and case size. | • Gaming → high‑end GPU & CPU
• Workstation → powerful CPU, ECC RAM, multi‑GPU
• Everyday use → mid‑range CPU, integrated graphics | | **What’s your budget?** | Keeps you from overspending or underspending. | • Set a hard cap (e.g., $800).
• Allocate 40% to GPU, 30% to CPU, 20% to storage, 10% to peripherals. | | **Do you have a preferred form factor?** | Affects case size, cable management, and cooling options. | • ATX (standard) → most parts fit.
• Micro‑ATX / Mini‑ITX → smaller, quieter, but limited expansion. | | **Do you need a specific feature?** | e.g., RGB lighting, Wi‑Fi, or a particular port. | • List must‑haves vs nice‑to‑haves. | | **Do you want to upgrade later?** | Choose a motherboard with extra slots, PCIe lanes, and power phases. | • Look for “future‑proof” boards (e.g., 12‑phase VRMs). | **Tools & Resources** - **PCPartPicker** – Build lists, price tracking, compatibility checks. - **Reddit r/buildapc** – Community advice, build reviews. - **YouTube channels** – Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents, Paul's Hardware. --- ### 2. Gather Your Parts | Component | Typical Choices | What to Look For | |-----------|-----------------|------------------| | **CPU** | AMD Ryzen 5/7, Intel Core i5/i7 | Clock speed, core count, cache, TDP | | **Motherboard** | B550 / X570 (AMD), B460 / Z590 (Intel) | Socket type, chipset, form factor, BIOS version | | **RAM** | DDR4 16–32 GB, 3200–3600 MHz | Capacity, speed, latency, dual‑channel | | **GPU** | NVIDIA RTX 3060/3070, AMD RX 6600/6700 | VRAM, memory bandwidth, power draw | | **Storage** | NVMe SSD (PCIe 3.0/4.0), SATA SSD/HDD | Capacity, read/write speeds, endurance | | **Power Supply (PSU)** | 650–850 W, 80+ Gold | Modular cables, efficiency, headroom | | **Case** | Mid‑tower, Mini‑ITX, or custom | Airflow, cable management, size | | **Cooling** | Stock cooler, aftermarket air cooler, AIO liquid | Compatibility, noise level, airflow | | **Operating System** | Windows 10/11, Ubuntu, etc. | License cost, driver support | > **Tip:** Use PCPartPicker to automatically check for compatibility and price alerts. --- ### 3. Prepare Your Workspace 1. **Clean, flat surface** – Avoid clutter. 2. **Anti‑static wrist strap** – Ground yourself or use an anti‑static mat. 3. **Tools** – Phillips screwdriver, tweezers, cable ties, thermal paste (if not pre‑applied). 4. **Lighting** – Good visibility reduces mistakes. --- ### 4. Assemble the Motherboard 1. **Install the CPU** - Lift the socket lever. - Align the CPU (triangle marker) with the socket. - Gently place it; lock the lever. 2. **Apply Thermal Paste** (if needed) - Small pea‑size dot in the center. 3. **Install the CPU Cooler** - Follow cooler instructions (fan orientation, mounting screws). 4. **Insert RAM** - Open the slots, align the notch, press until clicks. 5. **Mount the M.2 SSD** (if using) - Screw it into the M.2 slot, secure with a screw. --- ### 5. Install the Motherboard into the Case 1. **Place I/O Shield** – Insert into the back panel. 2. **Align Motherboard** – Match screw holes with standoffs. 3. **Secure with Screws** – Tighten evenly. --- ### 6. Install Power Supply 1. **Position PSU** – Usually at the bottom rear. 2. **Secure with Screws** – Align with case cutouts. 3. **Route Cables** – Keep them tidy; use cable management holes. --- ### 7. Add Storage & GPU | Step | Action | |------|--------| | **SATA SSD/HDD** | Mount in drive bay, connect SATA data + power cables. | | **NVMe SSD** | Already installed on motherboard. | | **GPU** | Insert into the top PCIe x16 slot, secure with screws. | | **Connect GPU Power** | Attach 8‑pin or 6‑pin cables from PSU. | --- ### 8. Connect Front Panel & Peripherals | Connector | Typical Pinout | |-----------|----------------| | **Power Switch** | 2 pins | | **Reset Switch** | 2 pins | | **Power LED** | 2 pins | | **USB 3.0** | 4 pins | | **Audio** | 5 pins | | **HDMI/DisplayPort** | 2 pins | > **Tip:** Refer to the motherboard manual for exact pin locations. --- ### 9. Cable Management - **Tidy up** – Use zip ties or Velcro straps. - **Ensure airflow** – Keep cables out of the way of fans. - **Label cables** – Helps with future upgrades or troubleshooting. --- ### 10. First Boot & BIOS Setup 1. **Power on** – Press the case power button. 2. **Enter BIOS** – Press `Delete` or `F2` during POST. 3. **Check** – - CPU, RAM, storage detected. - Boot order set to SSD. 4. **Save & Exit** – Usually `F10`. --- ### 11. Install Operating System | OS | Installation Steps | |----|---------------------| | **Windows 10/11** | 1. Create bootable USB (Rufus). 2. Boot from USB. 3. Follow wizard. | | **Ubuntu** | 1. Create bootable USB (balenaEtcher). 2. Boot from USB. 3. Install. | > **Tip:** Keep drivers handy (especially GPU drivers). --- ### 12. Install Drivers & Updates 1. **Motherboard chipset** – Download from manufacturer. 2. **GPU drivers** – NVIDIA GeForce Experience or AMD Radeon Software. 3. **Wi‑Fi/Bluetooth** – If using onboard modules. 4. **Windows Update** – Install all critical updates. --- ### 13. Test & Benchmark - **Stress test** – Prime95 (CPU), FurMark (GPU). - **Benchmark** – 3DMark, Cinebench, UserBenchmark. - **Monitor temperatures** – HWMonitor, MSI Afterburner. --- ### 14. Troubleshooting Common Issues | Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix | |---------|--------------|-----| | **No POST / No display** | Loose GPU, missing power cable, wrong BIOS settings | Re‑seat GPU, check cables, reset BIOS | | **Random reboots** | Overheating, insufficient PSU | Clean fans, add more cooling, upgrade PSU | | **Blue Screen** | Driver conflict, faulty RAM | Update drivers, run MemTest86 | | **Slow performance** | Bottlenecked CPU/GPU, inadequate cooling | Upgrade component, improve airflow | --- ### 15. Maintenance & Upgrades - **Dust cleaning** – Every 3–6 months. - **Thermal paste replacement** – Every 2–3 years. - **Upgrade RAM** – Add or replace modules. - **Add SSD** – Install additional SATA or NVMe drives. - **Upgrade GPU** – Swap for newer model. --- ## Quick Checklist - [ ] CPU, cooler, RAM, motherboard, PSU, case, GPU, storage - [ ] Anti‑static precautions - [ ] Cable management - [ ] BIOS settings - [ ] OS installation - [ ] Driver updates - [ ] Benchmark & stress test --- ### Final Words Building a PC is a rewarding project that gives you full control over performance, aesthetics, and future upgrades. Take your time, double‑check every connection, and enjoy the process! If you hit a snag, feel free to ask for help—there’s a huge community ready to assist. Happy building!
